subject: astronomy
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Stars appear to move across the night sky from east to west mainly because:
options: The Earth rotates on its axis from west to east
questions.explain: The apparent nightly motion of the stars is caused by the Earth's west-to-east rotation.

questions.q: The magnification of a telescope is found by:
options: Dividing the focal length of the objective by that of the eyepiece
Dividing the aperture by the focal length
Adding the focal lengths of the objective and eyepiece
questions.explain: Magnification equals objective focal length divided by eyepiece focal length.

questions.q: A refracting telescope forms its image using a:
questions.explain: A refractor uses a convex objective lens to gather and focus light; a reflector uses a mirror.

questions.q: On the celestial sphere, the celestial equator is:
options: A projection of the Earth's equator onto the sky
The path the Sun appears to follow over a year
The line joining the celestial poles
questions.explain: The celestial equator is the Earth's equator projected outward onto the celestial sphere.

questions.q: In the altitude-azimuth (horizontal) coordinate system, altitude measures:
options: The angle of an object above the horizon
The compass direction along the horizon
questions.explain: Altitude is the angle above the horizon, from 0 degrees at the horizon to 90 degrees at the zenith.

questions.q: Light pollution is a problem for astronomers because it:
options: Brightens the night sky and hides faint objects
questions.explain: Artificial light scatters in the atmosphere, washing out faint stars and reducing contrast.

options: The blurring and twinkling of images caused by atmospheric turbulence
questions.explain: Seeing describes image steadiness; turbulent air makes stars twinkle and blurs fine detail.

questions.q: Why do observatories often place very large telescopes on high mountains?
options: To be closer to the stars
To get above much of the atmosphere, reducing absorption and improving seeing
questions.explain: High, dry mountain sites have thinner, more stable air and less light pollution, improving observations.

questions.q: The constellations of the zodiac are special because:
options: The Sun, Moon and planets appear to move through them along the ecliptic
They are the brightest in the sky
questions.explain: The zodiac constellations lie along the ecliptic, the band through which the Sun, Moon and planets move.

questions.q: In the horizontal coordinate system, azimuth measures the:
options: Compass bearing around the horizon (usually from north)
questions.explain: Azimuth is measured around the horizon, conventionally clockwise from due north.

questions.q: A reflecting telescope gathers light using a:
questions.explain: A reflector uses a concave primary mirror, avoiding the lens problems of large refractors.

questions.q: Coordinated Universal Time (UT/GMT) is based on the local time at:
questions.explain: Universal Time is the mean solar time at the Greenwich meridian, the basis for world time zones.
